Shade their screen share. Keep your dark mode.

Safelight is a translucent rectangle for your Mac. Put it by hand over the light-mode screen someone is sharing on Zoom or Teams. Your terminal, browser and every other dark app stay exactly as they are.

Safelight — drag here, lock when done

Hold back the light, by hand.

In a darkroom you dodge a print by holding a card over the one patch that’s getting too much light. Safelight works the same way. It doesn’t know what Zoom is and doesn’t read your screen. It’s a coloured pane you place where the glare is.

That means it stays put. If the share moves or you resize the call, move the tint too. It takes a few seconds, and nothing else on your screen gets touched.

Show and hide
The switch at the top of the menu takes the tint away and brings it back. Its size and position are kept, so it returns exactly where you left it.
Move & Resize
Unlocking gives the tint a title bar to drag and edges to pull. While it’s unlocked it catches your clicks, the way any window would.
Done Moving
Locking removes the handles and lets every click pass straight through to the app underneath. You keep working; the tint just sits on top.
Stays out of the way
It lives in the menu bar with no Dock icon. It can float above other windows, follows you across Spaces, and remembers tint and placement between launches.

Make a test strip.

Printers expose a strip in steps to find the right time. Do the same with opacity: anywhere from 5% to 80%, in any colour, with Amber, Blue and Gray presets to start from. This second demo has its own controls and remembers its own settings.

Safelight — drag here, lock when done

A rectangle, and nothing cleverer.

What it does

  • Draws one translucent coloured rectangle, wherever you put it.
  • Lets you pick any colour, and opacity from 5% to 80%.
  • Shows and hides without forgetting its place.
  • Passes clicks through when locked.
  • Saves tint, position and size locally on your Mac.

What it doesn’t

  • Convert light apps to dark mode.
  • Find, track or snap to the shared window.
  • Read, record or upload anything on your screen.
  • Change your display brightness or colour settings.
  • Need an account. There isn’t one.

Build it in Xcode.

There’s no signed download yet. Safelight is a single SwiftUI file you build and run yourself; the source lives in the Sunglasses repository, which is its working name.

  1. Clone the source.

    git clone https://github.com/colefoster/Sunglasses.git

  2. Open it in Xcode. If you only have SunglassesApp.swift, create a new macOS App project and use that file as the app’s entry point.

  3. Choose My Mac as the run destination and press ⌘R. A sun icon appears in the menu bar; there’s no Dock icon.

  4. Click the icon, choose Move & Resize, drag the tint over the bright share, then click the icon again and choose Done Moving.

The current source uses the macOS 14 form of SwiftUI’s onChange. If Xcode refuses to build for a macOS 13 target, raise the deployment target to 14 or adjust those calls.
